steps: Step 1, Meet three letters and the three short vowels. The letter ب is read b: بَ (ba, with fatha, a small slash above), بِ (bi, with kasra, a small slash below), بُ (bu, with damma, a small curl above). Say each sound aloud three times.

Step 2, Do the same with ت and ا. تَ (ta), تِ (ti), تُ (tu). The letter ا (alif) carries the vowel sound: أَ (a), إِ (i), أُ (u). Read this row slowly, pointing at each mark: بَ تَ أَ، بِ تِ إِ، بُ تُ أُ.

Step 3, Join letters into real words. بَاب [door] has the long vowel alif. بِنْت [girl] and تَمْر [dates] show the little circle called sukun (ْ), which means no vowel on that letter. Sound them out: ba-b, bin-t, tam-r.

Step 4, Practise a tiny question and answer. Teacher: مَا هَذَا؟ [What is this?] Child: هَذَا بَاب. [This is a door.] Teacher: وَمَا هَذَا؟ [And what is this?] Child: هَذَا تَمْر. [This is dates, the fruit.] Point at pictures as you ask and answer.

Step 5, Spot the common error. A learner reads بِ as ba, ignoring the kasra under the letter. Correction: a mark below means i, so بِ is bi. Another error is writing بَاب as three separate letters ب ا ب; in a word the letters join from right to left.

Step 6, Your turn: read these aloud, then write the word for house. تُ، تِ، بَ، بُ. Model answer: tu, ti, ba, bu. The word for house is بَيْت [house], read bayt; check you wrote ب first on the right, then ي, then ت.
Step 1, Say the first vowels: अ आ इ ई उ ऊ ए ऐ ओ औ. Say each sound slowly: a, aa, i, ee, u, oo, e, ai, o, au. Trace each letter in the air with your finger, and write the top line (shirorekha) first.
Step 2, Link vowels to words. अ से अनार [A for pomegranate], आ से आम [Aa for mango], इ से इमली [I for tamarind], उ से उल्लू [U for owl]. Say the full line each time, like a chant: अ से अनार।

Step 3, Say the first consonants: क ख ग घ. क से कमल [K for lotus], ख से खरगोश [Kh for rabbit], ग से गमला [G for flower pot], घ से घर [Gh for house]. Notice that each consonant carries a short a sound.

Step 4, Write with a headline. Every letter in क, ख, ग, घ hangs from a line drawn on top, called शिरोरेखा [the headline]. Write each letter three times: क क क, ख ख ख. Then read your line aloud: कमल, खरगोश, घर.

Step 5, Fix an error. A learner writes the letters of कमल without the top line and reads क as k with no vowel. Correction: draw the line on top of every letter, and say each consonant with its short a: ka-ma-la, then read the whole word as कमल [lotus].
Step 6, Your turn: say and write च छ ज with one word each. Model answer: च से चम्मच [spoon], छ से छाता [umbrella], ज से जहाज़ [ship]. Write each letter three times with its headline.

Step 1, Learn fruit and food words. تُفَّاحٌ [apples], مَوْزٌ [bananas], بُرْتُقَالٌ [oranges], عِنَبٌ [grapes], خُبْزٌ [bread], حَلِيبٌ [milk], مَاءٌ [water], أَرُزٌّ [rice]. Show picture cards and say each word with the right shape in your mouth.

Step 2, Say what you like. أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحَ. [I like apples.] أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ. [I like bananas.] لَا أُحِبُّ الْحَلِيبَ. [I do not like milk.] The thing liked ends with a fatha sound: التُّفَّاحَ، الْمَوْزَ، الْحَلِيبَ.

Step 3, Ask a friend. هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْعِنَبَ؟ [Do you like grapes?] نَعَمْ، أُحِبُّهُ. [Yes, I like it.] لَا، لَا أُحِبُّهُ. [No, I do not like it.] Ask three classmates and record their answers on a tally sheet.

Step 4, Ask for food politely. Child: أُرِيدُ خُبْزًا مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. [I want some bread, please.] Seller: تَفَضَّلْ. [Here you are.] Child: شُكْرًا. [Thank you.] Seller: عَفْوًا. [You're welcome.] Replace خُبْزًا with مَاءً [water] or حَلِيبًا [milk].

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحُ with a damma ending. Correction: after أُحِبُّ the thing liked takes fatha, so say أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحَ. Remember to speak to a girl with مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.

Step 6, Your turn: say you like oranges and do not like rice, then ask for water. Model answer: أُحِبُّ الْبُرْتُقَالَ. لَا أُحِبُّ الْأَرُزَّ. أُرِيدُ مَاءً مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. [I like oranges. I do not like rice. I want water, please.]

Step 1, Learn the order of a Hindi sentence: who, what, action. मीना किताब पढ़ती है। [Meena reads a book.] Here मीना is the doer, किताब is the thing, पढ़ती है is the action. The action comes at the end.

Step 2, Make more sentences. रवि फुटबॉल खेलता है। [Ravi plays football.] माँ रोटी बनाती है। [Mother makes roti.] मैं पानी पीता हूँ। [I drink water, said by a boy.] मैं पानी पीती हूँ। [I drink water, said by a girl.]

Step 3, End sentences correctly. A full stop in Hindi is a vertical line। not a dot. Write: बच्चे स्कूल जाते हैं। [Children go to school.] Check that every sentence ends with the vertical line, and leave a space between words.

Step 4, Describe a picture. चित्र में एक लड़की है। [In the picture there is a girl.] वह फूल तोड़ती है। [She picks a flower.] पास में एक कुत्ता है। [Nearby there is a dog.] वह भौंकता है। [He barks.] Look at each picture and say three sentences.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes पढ़ती मीना किताब है. Correction: मीना किताब पढ़ती है। The action word should be at the end. Also check that the verb matches the doer: लड़का खेलता है, लड़की खेलती है.
Step 6, Your turn: write two sentences about a boy who drinks milk and a girl who reads. Model answer: लड़का दूध पीता है। लड़की किताब पढ़ती है। [The boy drinks milk. The girl reads a book.]

Step 1, Read this short passage I wrote. أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْمَدْرَسَةَ. فِي صَفِّي عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا. مُعَلِّمَتِي تَقْرَأُ لَنَا قِصَّةً كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. [I love school. In my class there are twenty students. My teacher reads us a story every day.] Read it twice, then underline the numbers.

Step 2, Find the key words. الْمَدْرَسَةُ [school], صَفٌّ [class], طَالِبٌ [student], قِصَّةٌ [story], كُلَّ يَوْمٍ [every day]. Say what each sentence is about before answering. The first is about liking school, the second about the class, the third about the story.

Step 3, Answer questions with a full sentence. كَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الصَّفِّ؟ [How many students are in the class?] فِي الصَّفِّ عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا. [In the class there are twenty students.] مَاذَا تَقْرَأُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ؟ [What does the teacher read?] تَقْرَأُ قِصَّةً. [She reads a story.]

Step 4, Ask a when-question. مَتَى تَقْرَأُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ الْقِصَّةَ؟ [When does the teacher read the story?] تَقْرَأُهَا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. [She reads it every day.] Notice how the answer repeats words from the text, which proves you found it in the passage.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student answers the question كَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الصَّفِّ؟ with the single word كَثِيرٌ [many]. Correction: go back to the text; the number is عِشْرُونَ, so the full answer is عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا. Guessing is not reading.

Step 6, Your turn: answer who reads us a story and where is the class. Model answer: مُعَلِّمَتِي تَقْرَأُ لَنَا قِصَّةً. [My teacher reads us a story.] صَفِّي فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [My class is at school.] Check you copied the spelling.

Step 1, Describe your morning in the present. أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ. [I wake up at seven o'clock.] أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي. [I wash my face.] أَتَنَاوَلُ الْفُطُورَ. [I have breakfast.] أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [I go to school.] Say them in order.

Step 2, Describe the rest of the day. أَعُودُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ. [I return home.] أَكْتُبُ وَاجِبِي. [I do my homework.] أَلْعَبُ مَعَ أَخِي. [I play with my brother.] أَنَامُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ. [I sleep at nine o'clock.]

Step 3, Describe a trip to the beach in the past. ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. [We went to the beach.] لَعِبْتُ بِالرَّمْلِ. [I played with the sand.] سَبَحَ أَخِي فِي الْبَحْرِ. [My brother swam in the sea.] كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا. [The weather was beautiful.]

Step 4, Compare present and past. الْيَوْمَ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [Today I go to school.] أَمْسِ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. [Yesterday I went to the beach.] The present verb begins with أَ for I; the past verb ends with تُ for I.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says أَمْسِ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. Correction: أَمْسِ [yesterday] needs the past, so say أَمْسِ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. Match the time word with the right verb form every time.

Step 6, Your turn: write about your morning and yesterday's trip, one sentence each. Model answer: أَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا وَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. أَمْسِ ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ وَلَعِبْتُ بِالرَّمْلِ. [I wake up early and go to school. Yesterday we went to the beach and I played in the sand.]

Step 1, Present your friend with name and age. Voici mon ami Karim. [Here is my friend Karim.] Il a huit ans. [He is eight years old.] Voici mon amie Inès. [Here is my friend Inès.] Elle a neuf ans. [She is nine years old.] Use il for a boy and elle for a girl.

Step 2, Describe what he or she looks like. Karim est grand et il a les cheveux noirs. [Karim is tall and has black hair.] Inès est petite et elle a les yeux bleus. [Inès is small and has blue eyes.] Notice petite takes an e because Inès is a girl.

Step 3, Describe character and likes. Karim est gentil et drôle. [Karim is kind and funny.] Il aime le football. [He likes football.] Inès est sportive. [Inès is sporty.] Elle aime la danse. [She likes dancing.] Add one thing you do together.

Step 4, A short dialogue. Maman : Comment est ton ami ? [What is your friend like?] Léo : Il est grand et très sympa. [He is tall and very nice.] Maman : Comment s'appelle-t-il ? [What is his name?] Léo : Il s'appelle Karim. [His name is Karim.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says Inès est grand. Correction: Inès est grande, because Inès is a girl and the adjective adds an e. Another slip is Il a neuf ans for a person who is nine and called Inès; say Elle a neuf ans.

Step 6, Your turn: present a friend named Samir, ten years old, short, kind, who likes drawing. Model answer: Voici mon ami Samir. Il a dix ans. Il est petit et gentil. Il aime dessiner. [Here is my friend Samir. He is ten. He is small and kind. He likes drawing.]

Step 1, A noun (संज्ञा) names a person, animal, thing or place. Each Hindi noun is masculine (पुल्लिंग) or feminine (स्त्रीलिंग). लड़का [boy] and घोड़ा [horse] are masculine. लड़की [girl] and चिड़िया [bird] are feminine.

Step 2, Use the ending as a clue. Many masculine nouns end in ा: लड़का, कमरा [room], बस्ता [bag]. Many feminine nouns end in ी: रोटी, कुर्सी, घड़ी [watch]. Make pairs: बेटा and बेटी, घोड़ा and घोड़ी. Say them aloud.

Step 3, Learn the exceptions. पानी [water], हाथी [elephant] and दही [curd] end in ी but are masculine: हाथी बड़ा है। [The elephant is big.] मेज़ [table] and किताब [book] are feminine: किताब अच्छी है। [The book is good.]

Step 4, Show gender through the verb. लड़का खेलता है। [The boy plays.] लड़की खेलती है। [The girl plays.] The verb ending changes from ता to ती. Sort these: फूल, मेज़, पेड़, कुर्सी. Masculine: फूल, पेड़. Feminine: मेज़, कुर्सी.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says यह मेज़ अच्छा है। Correction: यह मेज़ अच्छी है। because मेज़ is feminine. Another says पानी ठंडी है। Correction: पानी ठंडा है। because पानी is masculine.

Step 6, Your turn: name the gender of घड़ी, बस्ता, चिड़िया and घोड़ा. Model answer: घड़ी is feminine, बस्ता is masculine, चिड़िया is feminine, घोड़ा is masculine. Then write: घड़ी छोटी है। [The watch is small.] with the matching ending.
